en: Om, salutations to Śrī Gaṇeśa. I bow to Mukunda, who is full of bliss, whose lotus feet rest upon the lap of Vṛndāvana, who is worshipped by hosts of gods, the most excellent among the gods, praised by the multitude, who possesses a moon-like face, and whose form is slow with grace. The two brothers named Mukunda, Rāma, and Kṛṣṇa were born in former times.

May the prostration offered at the pair of feet of the venerable Puruṣottama—the ocean of jewels consisting of poetry, the Vedas, the Śāstras, and so forth—swiftly bestow purity upon the words of the scriptures and treatises. (2–3) Having churned the ocean of the Āgamas by the grace of my noble gurus, this compendium of the letters of the Mātṛkā is composed by the illustrious Bhānu. (4) Now, the syllable *Oṃ*...

The names of *Oṃ*: Oṃkāra, Tāraka, Avyakta, Vedādya, Praṇava, Avyaya, Dhruva, Tāra, Śiva, Mūla, Jyotis, and Śākhādika are remembered [as its names]. (5) The names of the letter *A*: Śrīkaṇṭha, Keśava, Kīrti, Nivṛtti, Amṛtā, Laghu, Pūrṇodarī, Mātṛkādya, Svarādya, and Amṛteśvara. (6) [Also] Kālādya and Keśavāṅga.

Mṛteśa, the first, shall be [the letter] *ka*; that which begins with the vowel *a* is to be known as Nyāsa. Now, the names of the vowels (*ākāra*): indeed, the vowel *a* is considered the Guru. 7. The vowel *ā* is Vāsudeva; Kānti is remembered as Nārāyaṇa. Ananta is Pratiṣṭhā, and likewise Virajā is Mānadā. 8. Dīrgha is Caturmukha, and Ādita (Ā) is remembered as Nārāyaṇa.

I (0): Ikāra is Mādhava, Sūkṣma, Pāñcajanya, and Mukhāṅkura. Pūṣan, Vidyut, Dvibindu, and Catuṣṭi are remembered as Śālmalika; he is the third right eye, Gandharva, and Parameśvara. Ī (0): Īkāra is Trimūrti, Lolākṣī, and Vāmalocana; he is Tuṣṭi, Puṣṭi, Nṛsiṃhāstra, and Govinda is the fourth.

Indramūrti, Mahāmāyā, Asureśa, and Śānti are proclaimed [as the deities of the letter *i*]. || 0 || At the letter *u*, there is Vartulākṣī, Yāmyakarṇa, and Rameśvara. || 12 || Amareśa, Dhṛti, Viṣṇu, Indhikā, and Puṣṭi; Gajāṅkuśa, Manmatha, Vijaya, and Vighnahāraka. || 13 || [The fifth: At the letter *ū*, there is Dīpikā and Madhusūdana; Vāmāṅga... [and so forth]. || 0 || at the letter *ū*. Makarṇa is known as Dīrgha and Śāntirati; Indravāyu is indeed Dīrghaghoṇa, while Ṣaṇmukha is considered the Lord (Adhīśa).

The sixth vowel is said to be *ṛ*. (0) The letter *ṛ* is *Sumukhī*, *Kriyā*, (15) *Dakṣanāsā*, *Bhārabhūti*, *Tapanī*, *Recikā*, *Dhṛti*, *Trivikrama*, *Ripughna*, *Varmin*, and *Vigrahanāyaka*. (16) The seventh [vowel] is *ṛ*. (0)
Sthūṇa, Atharva, Śaśinī, Mocikā, and Dayā; Vāmanāsā, Tithīśa, Gomukhī, Sthāṇu, and Īśvara.
Vāmana shall be Amṛteśa, Śrīdhara shall be Tripurāntaka, and Devajña is declared as the eighth: Ḷ (0).

The letter *ḷ* is, according to the view of Candrikā, located on the left cheek; it is Sthāṇu, Dīrghajihvā, and the knower of the three Vedas (18). It is Ekāṅga, Vajradaṇḍa, Vyomārddha, and the ninth vowel (19). It is proclaimed by the wise as Medhā, Devasūti, and Śrīdhara. [The letter] *ḹ* (0). The letter *ḹ* is on the left cheek; it is Kubera, the Eye (20), Sūkṣma, Arddhi, Ghorahara, Kuṇḍodarī, Hṛṣīkeśa, and Saharṣā.

Cagaṇeśa is the trikaṇṭaka (three-thorned). Nīlāṅghri is declared as the tenth. The letter E (E) is situated in the triangle; it resides on the upper lip, is Jhiṃṭirīśa, and likewise resides in faith, knowledge, and the mind. Jagajjyoti, Padmanābha, and Śaktika are [the next]; Ūrdhvakeśī and Jyotsnā are proclaimed as the eleventh. The letter Ai (Ai) is Bhautika.

Jyādhara is remembered [as the first]. Vāgīśa, Praṇava, Varma, Bhayada, Śrī, and Mṛta likewise [are the next six]. Dāmodara is the twelfth; likewise Vikṛtānanā. Oṃ, Aṅgasaṃjñā, and Āpyāyanī likewise [are the following]. Ūrdhvadaṃtā, Alija, and Sadyojāta are remembered. Jvālāmukhī, Vāsudeva, and Lakṣmī are the three mātrās. Tra... [the remainder of the verse is missing].

The thirteenth is considered the Lord of Mantras (Maṃtreśa), the Lord of Matras (Mātreśa), and the Praṇava. The vowel *au* is declared to be Vyāpinī; it is the limb of Nṛsiṃha and Sarasvatī. (27) Below that is Aghoradantī, Bhijonetrā, Laghu, and Ulkāmukhī. Murāri, Māyāvī, Aṅgada, and Anugraheśvara are likewise mentioned by the learned as the fourteenth Saṃkarṣaṇas. The vowel *aṃ* is the [final] vowel. (28) *(Note: The text provided contains a mix of Sanskrit phonemes and their mystical designations. The translation reflects the sequence and associations given in the source.)*

(-) Ścapūrṇā is Aprīti; Śaśī is Mṛta. ||29|| Suśrīmukhī is indeed Ūrdhvadanta, known as Pradyumna; Akrūra is Manmathāṅga, Kaṇṭhacarī, Vyomarūpī, and Nigūḍhaka. ||30|| Pūrṇā is Pañcadaśa; (0) this is called Svara, and Rati is the vowel 'a'. [The letter] situated at the end of the sentence is Mahāsena, and [the letter] with the luster of a maiden’s breast is Kanyā. ||31|| Pūrṇāmukhī is Anantā, and Viṣṇu...
Trā, Niruddha, Kau, Pūrṇa, Amṛta, and the one ending with Avisarga; Viraja is the sixteenth vowel. Now, the names beginning with Ka: 32.
The letter *ka* is Kāmaga, Krodhin, Yādava, Āveśa, Jaya, Yāmyakarṇa, Ka-ja, Cakrin, Mahīkanya, and Aṣurāri.
Sṛṣṭi, Saptadaśa, Sparśādya, Kha, Atharavarṇaka, Ṛddhi, Caṇḍīśvara, Durgā, Khaga, Nandī, Sarasvatī; Dakṣiṇa, Kūrpara, Kheṭa, Kaiṭabhāri, Aṣṭādaśa, Mātaṅga,
Saṃhāra, Ga, Gārṇaka, Smṛti, Pañcāntaka, Sarvasiddhi, Śārṅgin, and Prabhā.

Gomukha, Gajakuṃbha, [—], Siṃha, and Gaṇeśvara; ||36|| likewise, the nineteenth is Maṇimān stationed on the right. Gha (0), the letter Gha (—), Medhā, Gaurī, and Śivottama; ||37|| Aṃgulīmūlaka, Satya, Khaḍgīśa, and Ghana; the twentieth is Varāha, and Ādiṅga; Ṅa, the letter Ṅa is known as Caṇḍī, Kānti, and then Ekaru.

The letter *ḍra* is located at the tip of the right index finger; it is associated with the conch (*śaṅkhin*), has a neuter face, and is nasal (*anunāsika*). (39) Bhadreśvara is proclaimed as the twenty-first mantra-power (*mantra-śakti*). The letter *ca* is Citracārī, Calakṣmī, and Kūrma; it is also *cañcala*.
(40) Halī, Bāṇī, Ātmaśakti, Bhūteṭ, Tāreśa, and Candraka—these are held in the left hand as the twenty-second [power]. The letter *cha* is then Triviṃ...

Daka (41). Vāmakūrpara (the left elbow) becomes Muśalī; Mātā, Vilāsinī, Paripūrṇa, Ekanetra, Jvālī, and Āśleṣmā likewise (42). Then Trayoviṃśa and Dyuti. Ja (0). The letter *Ja* is Janaka, Sthira, Vijaya, and Jīvana; the letter *Jha* is Jayanta and Caturānana (43). Vāmāṅga (the left limb) is located at Maṇibandha; Sthamātṛka becomes Śūlī. Caturviṃśa...

Śo|| Jha (0)|| The letter *Jha* is Drāviṇī, Svastika, and Sthiti. ||44|| With the root of the left finger is Śī, Sthirā, and the form of Ajeśvara. Vitsthāta, Viraja, Khaṇḍa, Lambodara, and Tha-ārṇaka. ||45|| Ña (0)|| Located at the tip of the left finger is Soma; Sarveśa is known as Nandana. Sadharma and Anunāsa; Jñaptiga is considered to be Aṅkuśī. ||46||

The stainless one (nirañjana) is the Nāgarī Siddhi, described as Viśva. This is the twenty-sixth [letter]. Ṭa (0). The letter Ṭha is Rāja-aṅkuśa, Jarā. Someśvara is the Nāgarī Vimalā-bhṛtā. It consists of the first part of the right foot and the crescent moon of the young moon. This is the twenty-seventh, Kunda. Ṭha (0). The letter Tha is Lāṅgalīśvara, Sudhā-vi...

Duḥpālana, Ituna, Nandaja, and Sunanda; ||49|| Caṇḍa situated at the right knee, Mañjarī, and Dāruka; Ghaṭākāra and Phalāvaka—this is declared as the twenty-eighth [group]. ||50|| From the right ankle: Ārakeśa, Śānti, Nandī, and Smṛti; Ḍakāra, Vyāghrapāda, Ḍāmara, Agni, Adri, and Nāḍika. ||51|| Bhaumaja and Ūrūpi...
The twenty-ninth is known as Ṇīcai; this is declared to be Śubhāṃhi. Then the letter Ḍha is remembered as Nara. (52)

Residing on the big toe of the right foot is Ardhanārīśvara, born from the letter Ḍa; Aiśvarī, Vīriṇī, Ṛddhi, Śaṅkhanābhi, Nibha, Kṛti, Pūrṇa, Udānta, and Triṃśat are the names [of the letters] from Ṇa to Ṇa (Ṇa being the thirtieth). The letter Ṇa is Narakāntaka. Residing at the tip of the little toe of the right foot is Samṛddhi, who is Trivikrama. Umākānta, Rati, Kṛṣṇa, Nirvāṇa, and Triguṇa are considered [the names of the letters] from Ta to Ma.

The thirty-first [chapter] is indeed named Kākodarīḍhānta; [then there is] Ta (0) and that Tārṇaka. (55) Āṣāḍhī, Pūtanāśuddhi, Hari, and Vāmapadādika; Kāmika, Atīvrataraya, Dhātṛ, and Nīla are proclaimed. (56) The thirty-second.
The syllable *tha* is declared to be the water-pot (*kamaṇḍalu*) of Kṛṣṇabuddhi; Śobhanā Bhadrakālī stands upon his left knee, holding a staff and granting boons.

The Elder (Sthavira) is long-enduring, the thirty-third, and large-eyed. (58) The letter *Da* is Hlādinī, Satya, Buddhi, and Dhāti; Śūla resides in the left ankle, while Deveśa, Atri, and Yoginī are the thirty-fourth, the letter *La*. (59) The letter *Dha* is Mati and Sāttvata; Gomī, Dharma, Īśa, Dharaṇīśvara, and Sthāṇu reside at the end of the left ankle.

Prīti, Śaṅkhinī, Tuda, Nandī, and Janārdana. [This is] the thirty-fifth [chapter]. From the letter *na* come Gurjanī, Meṣa, and Śauri. The long vowel *ā* at the end of the left finger, the Earth-element (*bhūdhātu*), Rākā, and that which has the luster of poison. [This is] the thirty-sixth [chapter]. From the letter *pa* come Kālarātri and Amemate. [This is] the thirty-seventh [chapter]. From the letter *ya* comes Yāmyapā...
R̥ṣva, Padmanābha, Dakṣiṇa, Lohita, Saptatriṃśat, Viśvamūrti, Śūra, Padmeśa, and Pārthiva—[these are the thirty-seven]. 63.

*Tīkṣṇa* (the Sharp). Pha (0): The letter *Pha* is Vaikuṇṭha, the left side, Śiva, and Nala; it is Śikhī, Raudrī, and Kuṇḍanī, while *Phaṭkāra* is Janārdana. 64. *Pulla* is Pallava and Umā; thus there are thirty-eight [deities]. Ba (0): The letter *Ba* is Pṛṣṭhavaṃśa, Chagalaṇḍa, and Kapardinī. 65. Bhūdhara, Balavān, Vajramuṣṭi, and Puruṣottama; Surasa...

The letter *ka* (kledinī-bhādyaḥ) is remembered as the nectar-rayed moon; it is the forty-ninth, and its seed-syllable is *yī*. The letter *tha* (thobhā) is said to be the syllable *ma*; Viśvamūrti, the Lord of the Cosmic Egg, born from the navel, is the remover of fear. Nidrāklinnābhāravīra, Śubhadā, and Bhṛkuṭījayā constitute the fortieth; Bharadvāja is the letter *ma*, the first of the syllables beginning with *ma*. Mahākāla...

Bhāravīra, Staṃdrī, Vaikuṇṭha, Puruṣa; Vijayārka, Sudhāmān, Maṇḍala, Mādhava, Mṛḍa—these constitute the forty-first [group], with Maṃtreśa situated in the middle of the *tāra*. (Ya) The letter Ya, Śvasana, Bālī, Vasudhā, Sumukheśvarī;
Hṛdayastha, Tvagātmā, Mṛgeṃdra, Puruṣottama, Yamuneya—these constitute the forty-second [group].

*Pi* is hunger; *kṣu* is said to be the seed-syllable (*bīja*) of wind. *Ra* (0) is Revatī and the other [constellation]; it is considered the blood-element (*asṛgdhātu*), the Lord of Serpents (*bhujaṅgeśa*), powerful, and wrathful (*krodhinī*). 72. On the right shoulder is Tīvratejas; in the forty-third [position] is Hutāśana, the fire-seed-syllable (*vahni-bīja*); he is considered radiant (*rociṣman*) and Ruci. 73. *La* (0): the letter *la* is the flesh-element (*māṃsa-dhātu*); he resides on the hump (*kakutstha*).

The younger brother of the Strong One (Balarāma), the refuge, the one born of the earth, the one with dark garments—[these are the names]. 74. The wielder of the Pināka bow, the Lord, the one of lightness, the son of Umā, the one with the thunderbolt-like fist—this shall be the forty-fourth [chapter]; the seed of Indra, the action of the Bull. 75. The letter *Va*, the one belonging to Varuṇa, the child, the subtle one, the sword-bearer, the Lord of the Śavas, the giver of water; the one known as Medas situated on the left shoulder, the one belonging to Varuṇa, the swan, the spray.

Rau || 76 || Amṛteśa is the seed-syllable of nectar (sudhā-bīja); Drava is remembered as the aquatic one (jala-cara). The forty-fifth [consonant] ends with *la* (i.e., *ḷa*), and [the vowel] *śa* is zero (*śūnya*).

The letter Śa is the wind-god Vāyu. The bone-element (asthi-dhātu), Śaṅkukarṇa, and Varāha are remembered as its meditative objects (adhyāyanas). Saṃdhyāmṛtyu is the destroyer of poison, and Lakṣmī resides in his right hand. The forty-sixth is the letter Ṣa (Ṣaṃbau). The letter Ṣa is Śveta and Khara-mukha; it is remembered as the marrow-soul (majjātman), located in the left hand, and as the bull and Tatpuruṣa. Ghaṭā... [77-79]
The forty-seventh [chapter] concerns the sixfold form of Kāraṣaḍā, the bearer of the destruction of the Rakṣasas, and the six weapons of Vimalaprajñā.

The letter *Sa* (0) is Sahaja, Śveta, Haṃsa, Bhṛgu, Īśa, Samagra, Prabhā, Dīpta, Asya, Samaya, Satyānanda, and Himāṃśu. ||81|| It is the Śukradhātu, Satya, Sada, Dakṣapāda, and Vāsānaka; it is the forty-eighth (*Ha*). The letter *Ha* (0) is Nakulīśvara. ||82|| It is Hutāśa, Hākinī, Drāva, Hayātana, Sadāśiva, and Nī...

Lal-lakṣmāruṇa and Prāṇaheraṃba are located on the left foot. (83) The forty-ninth is the seed-syllable of space (*vyomabīja*): *la* (0). The letter *lā* is Śiveśvara; he is the abode of the individual soul (*jīvātman*), and likewise Vimalā and Asitā. (84) Amoghā is the fiftieth: *kṣa* (0). The syllable *kṣa* is the end of the Mātṛkā. Anantā, Vidyutā, Māyā, Saṃvarttakā, and Kṛtā—[these reside] in the fifty-first. (85) The fifty-second is the syllable *ha*; it is the supreme, the unmanifest (*avyakta*). It is the support of all mantras, the source of the three worlds, and the abode of the supreme self (*paramātman*). (86) The fifty-third is the syllable *kṣa*; it is the supreme, the unmanifest.
